state:
Goal `tools-server`: three of the chapter's eight features have their proofs,
`tools:server/behind-a-proxy-trusted-proxies`, `tools:server/mounts-which-file-answers-a-request` and
`tools:server/what-a-program-reads-about-its-door`. `bun nv proofs --owed --group tools:server` lists
the five still owed. Nothing is blocked, and the last slice changed no Rust beyond a `covers:` marker.

A `.nvst` case cannot name a mount (`crates/nvs-test/src/request.rs:67`), so a case for a mount feature
pins what the root mount reads; a `.nvsr` file beside an example or an attack names one with
`--MOUNT--`, the prefix on its first line and one capture on each line after it.

The three features left in the group owe `help`: the check reports that `# nvs ctl` and `# nvs service`
show no code although each has an indented usage block (`docs/reference/tools/25-server.md:296`), and
the sections that pass show a fenced one. Whether a fence is the whole difference is not checked.

backlog: `Core\Router::url` writes the mount prefix into a link exactly as the request carries it. The attack `tests/hostile/tools/server/what-a-program-reads-about-its-door/01-a-folder-name-that-looks-like-a-path.nvs` hands it the prefix `/%2e%2e` and prints links that begin with it, which a browser resolves out of the mount. Whether the boot expansion in `crates/nvs-config/src/mount.rs` can produce such a prefix from a folder name is not checked; `rule:routing/link-carries-the-mount-prefix` owns the answer.
